title: Coral and the Bubble Party
readingLevel: UK Reception–Year 1. Very short sentences, high-frequency words, a few sparkle words (mermaid, unicorn, seaweed, starfish, sneeze).

shipdoor.prompt: The door needs three things. Pick three.
shipdoor.wrongFeedback: The door stayed shut. What did Granny Tide say?

p1.text: Coral was a mermaid. She lived in a little cave under the sea. Her best friend was Splash. Splash was a unicorn. A unicorn who could swim! Today was the Bubble Party. Splash found a pearl in the sand. "Ooh," said Splash.

p2.text: Granny Tide was a very old turtle. "The party is at the Sunken Ship," she said. "But the door is locked. To open it, you need three things. A pearl. A singing shell. And a starfish. Not a crab. Crabs pinch." Splash laughed.

p3.text: "One more thing," said Granny Tide. "Swim through the seaweed. Do not swim past the sleepy shark. He sneezes." "Seaweed, not shark," said Coral. "A shark that sneezes!" said Splash. "Ha!"

p4.text: They swam to the sandy bay. A crab sat on a rock. Splash put the crab on his head. "A hat!" said Splash. The crab pinched his ear. "Ow!" said Splash. Coral giggled.

p5.text: Next, the shell garden. Shells of every colour! Coral held one to her ear. It sang a little song. "A singing shell!" said Coral. Splash tried one too. His shell went blub.

p6.text: By the rocks, a starfish waved. "Hello!" said the starfish. "Will you come to the party?" asked Coral. "Yes!" said the starfish. It stuck to Splash's nose. Everyone laughed.

p7.text: The path went two ways. Left, through the seaweed. Right, past the sleepy shark. "Sharks are funny," said Splash. "Let's go right!" Coral stopped. What had Granny Tide said?

p8a.text: They swam right, past the shark. Big mistake. The shark opened one eye. "Ah... ah... AH-CHOO!" The sneeze blew them all the way back. "Not the shark," said Coral. "The seaweed."

p8b.text: They swam left, through the seaweed. It tickled. Splash ate some seaweed. "Yum," he said. Then they saw it. The Sunken Ship! Bubbles floated up from inside. The party!

p9.text: The ship had a big wooden door. It was locked. Three little holes were in the door. "Three things," said Coral. "What did Granny Tide say?" Splash held up the crab. "Not the crab!" said Coral.

p10.text: Click! The door swung open. Bubbles everywhere! Fish danced. A jellyfish glowed like a lamp. Splash did a loop-the-loop. Coral laughed and laughed. It was the best party under the sea.

p11.text: Granny Tide swam in slowly. "You remembered," she said. Splash gave her a bubble. It popped on her nose. "Ha!" said Granny Tide. And they all danced until the moon came up.

Nothing new appears, nothing changes shape, no morphing, no flicker. Everything else in the picture stays exactly as it is.

p1.text: Coral is a mermaid. Splash can swim. Splash got a pearl.
p1.narration: Splash was a unicorn. A unicorn who could swim! He and Coral lived together in a little cave under the sea, and Coral was his best friend in the whole ocean. Today was the Bubble Party, and Splash had found the pearl lying in the sand. "Ooh," said Splash, holding it up to the light.

p2.text: "You need a pearl. A singing shell. And a starfish. Not a crab!"
p2.narration: That was Granny Tide, a very old turtle who knew everything. "The party is at the Sunken Ship," she said. "But the door is locked. To open it, you need three things." She said them again, slowly: a pearl, a singing shell, and a starfish. "Not a crab. Crabs pinch." Splash laughed so hard he blew a bubble.

p3.text: "Swim in the seaweed. Do not go past the shark. He sneezes!"
p3.narration: Granny Tide had one more thing to say, and that was it. "Seaweed, not shark," said Coral, to be sure she remembered. "A shark that sneezes!" said Splash. "Ha!" He thought that was the funniest thing he had ever heard.

p4.text: A crab sat on a rock. Splash put it on his head. "Ow!" said Splash.
p4.narration: They had swum all the way to the sandy bay, where the sunlight wobbled on the sand. The crab had been minding its own business. "A hat!" said Splash, very pleased with himself, right up until the crab pinched his ear. Coral giggled until her tail shook.

p5.text: Coral got a shell. It sang. "A singing shell!" said Coral.
p5.narration: This was the shell garden, where shells of every colour lay in rows like sweets in a shop. Coral had held the shell to her ear and it sang a tiny, tinkling song. Splash tried one too, and pressed it hard against his ear. His shell went blub.

p6.text: "Hello!" said the starfish. It stuck to Splash. Ha ha!
p6.narration: Down by the rocks, a cheerful orange starfish had been waving all five arms at once. "Will you come to the party?" Coral asked it politely. "Yes, yes, yes!" said the starfish, and stuck itself right onto Splash's nose. Everyone laughed, even the fish.

p7.text: "Go right!" said Splash. Coral stopped. What did Granny Tide say?
p7.narration: The path had split in two. To the left, tall seaweed swaying. To the right, a dark rocky arch where the sleepy shark lay snoring. "Sharks are funny," Splash had said. But Coral thought hard. What exactly had Granny Tide told them?

p8a.text: The shark went AH-CHOO! It blew them back. "Not the shark," said Coral.
p8a.narration: They had swum right, past the sleepy shark. Big mistake. The shark opened one enormous eye. "Ah... ah... ah..." and then the sneeze, which blew them head over tail all the way back to the fork in the path. "The seaweed," said Coral, straightening her hair.

p8b.text: Splash ate some seaweed. "Yum!" Then they saw the ship.
p8b.narration: They had swum left, through the seaweed forest, and the fronds tickled their sides as they passed. "Salty," said Splash, chewing. And there it was between the fronds at last: the Sunken Ship, with streams of bubbles floating up from inside. The party was already starting.

p9.text: It was locked. "Three things," said Coral. "Not the crab!"
p9.narration: The ship's big wooden door had three little round holes in it, and it was shut tight. Coral tried to remember. Splash held up the crab, which was still sitting on his head, and offered it to the door. "Not the crab!" said Coral again. What had Granny Tide said?

p10.text: Bubbles! Fish! A jellyfish lamp! Splash did a loop. Coral laughed.
p10.narration: Click! The door had swung wide open. Bubbles streamed out in every colour. Fish danced in rows, and a jellyfish glowed like a lamp, then another, and another. Splash did his loop-the-loop three times until he was dizzy. It was the best party under the sea.

p11.text: "You did it," she said. Splash gave her a bubble. Pop! "Ha!"
p11.narration: Granny Tide had swum in slowly, last of all, and her old eyes twinkled. "You remembered," she said. The bubble Splash gave her popped on the very tip of her nose. And they all danced, and danced, until the moon came up over the water.

p1.text: Coral was a mermaid with a shimmering green tail. She lived in a little cave under the sea, where the walls sparkled with shells. Her best friend was Splash, a unicorn who could swim faster than any fish. Today was the Bubble Party, and Splash had already found a pearl in the sand. "Ooh," he said. "Shiny."

p2.text: Granny Tide was the oldest turtle in the whole ocean. "The party is at the Sunken Ship," she said slowly. "But the door is locked tight. To open it, you will need three things. A pearl. A singing shell. And a starfish. Not a crab. Crabs pinch, and doors do not like being pinched." Splash laughed so hard he blew a bubble.

p3.text: "One more thing," said Granny Tide, wagging a wrinkly flipper. "Swim through the seaweed forest. Whatever you do, do not swim past the sleepy shark. He sneezes, and his sneezes are enormous." "Seaweed, not shark," said Coral carefully. "A shark that sneezes!" said Splash. "That is the funniest thing I have ever heard."

p4.text: They swam across the sandy bay, where the sunlight wobbled on the sand. A small red crab sat on a rock, minding its own business. Splash scooped it up and balanced it on his head. "Look! A hat!" said Splash. The crab pinched his ear, quite hard. "Ow!" said Splash. Coral giggled until her tail shook.

p5.text: Next came the shell garden, where shells of every colour lay in neat rows like sweets in a shop. Coral picked up a spiral shell and held it to her ear. It sang a tiny, tinkling song. "A singing shell!" said Coral. Splash tried one too, and pressed it hard against his ear. His shell went blub.

p6.text: Down by the rocks, a cheerful orange starfish waved all five arms at once. "Hello!" said the starfish. "Will you come to the party with us?" asked Coral politely. "Yes, yes, yes!" said the starfish, and it stuck itself right onto Splash's nose. Everyone laughed, even the fish.

p7.text: The sandy path split in two. To the left, a tall forest of swaying seaweed. To the right, a dark rocky arch where the sleepy shark lay snoring. "Sharks are funny," said Splash. "Let's go right and watch him sneeze!" Coral stopped and thought hard. What exactly had Granny Tide said?

p8a.text: They swam right, past the sleepy shark. Big mistake. The shark opened one enormous eye. "Ah... ah... ah... AH-CHOO!" The sneeze blew them head over tail, all the way back to the fork in the path. "Not the shark," said Coral, straightening her hair. "The seaweed."

p8b.text: They swam left, through the seaweed forest. The fronds tickled their sides as they passed. Splash nibbled some seaweed on the way. "Yum," he said. "Salty." Then, between the fronds, they saw it at last. The Sunken Ship! Streams of bubbles floated up from inside. The party was already starting.

p9.text: The ship had a big wooden door with three little round holes in it, and it was locked tight. "Three things," said Coral, remembering. "What exactly did Granny Tide say?" Splash held up the crab, which was still on his head. "Not the crab!" said Coral.

p10.text: Click! The door swung wide open. Bubbles streamed out in every colour. Fish danced in rows. A jellyfish glowed like a lamp, and then another, and another. Splash did a loop-the-loop, then two more, until he was dizzy. Coral laughed and laughed. It was the best party under the sea.

p11.text: Granny Tide swam in slowly, long after everyone else. "You remembered," she said, and her old eyes twinkled. Splash gave her a bubble. It popped on the very tip of her nose. "Ha!" said Granny Tide. And they all danced, and danced, until the moon came up over the water.
